# Landing Party {.unnumbered kicker="Field manual"}

Landing Party adds three factions to Nauvis. Two are corporations that land, mine, build factories and field armies of
their own. The third takes over biter spawners and breeds its own biters. All three compete with you for the planet,
and with each other.

They do not arrive at the start. Each one comes when your factory reaches a certain point, so each meets a factory
that can answer it. [Arrivals](arrivals.qmd) has the timeline.

## The factions

**Grubstake** comes first, around chemical science. It is a mining company that lives off your factory. It carries off
machines, skims your belts, robs your chests, strip-mines the ore under your outposts and claims ore you leave unmined.
It avoids defended ground, and the wild biters leave it alone. See [Grubstake](grubstake.qmd).

**Kessler-Hayashi** comes when you launch your first rocket. It is a security contractor, at war with you from the day it
lands. Its camps are walled and paved, and it pushes a line of posts out toward your base. It brings tanks,
railgunners and sieges with mortars and howitzers. See [Kessler-Hayashi](kessler-hayashi.qmd).

**Synthexis** comes when the wild biters' evolution reaches {{< var synthexis.arrive_evo >}}. It takes over a spawner
field far from you, feeds it on your pollution and sends waves of bred biters that pick their way into your defenses.
See [Synthexis](synthexis.qmd).

The corporations also fight each other. See [Rivals](rivals.qmd).

## What you get

Faction bases can be destroyed. Their wreckage holds parts you cannot make yourself. Crafting those parts unlocks
technologies built from their designs, and a command core from their wreckage lets you build a barracks and raise
[your own army](army.qmd). [Spoils](spoils.qmd) lists what drops where and what it unlocks.

## Before you start

- Landing Party needs Factorio {{< var mod.factorio >}} with Space Age. This manual describes version
  {{< var mod.version >}}.
- Chat notices are off by default. A faction's first landing and a destroyed faction base are always announced. Turn
  on **Chat notices** in the map settings to hear about everything else. See [Mod settings](reference.qmd#sec-settings).
- Each faction has a strength and an aggression setting, from ×{{< var settings.very_low >}} to
  ×{{< var settings.very_high >}}.

## Using this manual

Each faction's chapter opens with its own page of history, then how it lands, fights and grows, its unit tree and a
card for every unit it fields. [Reference](reference.qmd) has every unit and building in tables, the chat commands and
the settings. [Tips](tips.qmd) collects what works against each faction.

::: {.lore kicker="Freight Authority, Lane Registry" title="A surface, reclassified"}

::: {.dossier}
SURFACE
: Nauvis, the green one of the five. Charted once, by the Authority's survey tender *Carrow*, which stopped reporting
  on its third orbit in the Registry's ninth year and is carried as lost with all hands. Entry since: "uncharted,
  hazard".

LANES
: None registered. Freight on the inner lanes clears the planet by the margin Lane Rule 3 allows. No fee has ever been
  collected off it.

HAZARD REGISTER
: H-1, the indigenous fauna, class one, "breeds from smoke". H-3, "operator, unregistered": one engineer, name not
  supplied, building without a licence; first noted as a stain on the daylight side from the Aquilo run.

RECLASSIFICATION
: Form LR-7, "Surface activity confirmed. Reclassify as commercial", signed O. Brandt, Registrar, on the day a cargo
  rocket left the surface. Objections: none filed.

OPERATORS ON FILE
: Grubstake Inc. (file 209), Kessler-Hayashi Security (file 114), Synthexis (file 377). None holds a licence for the
  surface.

THIS HISTORY
: Compiled by M. Tanase, Clerk second grade, Lane Registry, from the three operators' own filings. The clerk has read
  all of them and vouches for none.
:::

The Authority keeps a sheet for every surface the lanes pass, and for most of the Registry's life the Nauvis sheet
held two lines. The first named the *Carrow*, a survey tender of forty tons that went into orbit there to chart the
ground and stopped reporting on its third pass; the Registry carries her as lost with all hands and has never been
able to say to what. The second line was the word *hazard*. Freight clears the planet by the margin Lane Rule 3
allows, and in nine years no operator asked the Lane Registry for anything closer, because nothing on Nauvis was for
sale. Vulcanus has its foundries and the demolishers the foundries pay cordons against. Fulgora has its scrap lots and
the storm season that ends them. On Gleba every living thing is somebody's lease, and Aquilo is an ice run with a
freighter schedule. Nauvis had the swarm, and the *Carrow*'s wreck.

What changed the sheet was smoke. A platform on the Aquilo run logged a stain on the daylight side, and the next pass
found it wider, with a radar sweeping under it and a flare at night that the duty officer entered as a refinery. The
Registry does not act on smoke. It acts on cargo, and when a rocket cleared the atmosphere carrying a manifest nobody
had filed, Registrar Brandt signed Form LR-7 within the hour. The surface became commercial, which means a place an
operator may land on with a licence. Three operators have landed on it since. None has applied.

::: {.pullquote cite="Form LR-7, Nauvis sheet, signed O. Brandt, Registrar"}
Surface activity confirmed. Reclassify as commercial.
:::

Grubstake's tender *Assay* was first down, with a radar, two drills and a handful of guards, the week the operator's
refinery lit; its Claims Agent filed a Notice of Intent to Claim from the ground, which the Registry stamped and could
do nothing about. Kessler-Hayashi waited for the rocket, as its contract says it may, and came down inside a surveyed
boundary with its guns already on the wall. Synthexis came last and told nobody, so that the Registry learned of its
trial from a Kessler-Hayashi site report that called it pest control. What the three have in common is in their own
filings, where each lists the operator's works as something it is entitled to. Grubstake's register carries the works
as unattended. In Kessler-Hayashi's contract they are cargo under its protection, and Synthexis's protocol, when the
Registry finally saw a copy, has them down as the control.

What the Registry can count, it counts. Each lander's descent is logged from the lanes, and by the log the two
corporations take turns, the one with fewer sites standing going next, and a rocket off the surface brings
Kessler-Hayashi's next lander down sooner than its schedule. The operator's first radar charted a wreck a little
way off that the Registry takes to be the *Carrow*. Her log has not been sent to the Authority, and the clerk has
written twice.

The clerk's own view, which the Registrar has asked her to keep off the sheet, is on this page because the sheet has no
column for it. The *Carrow* was lost to the swarm, the swarm now feeds on the operator's smoke, and two of the three
companies on file are paying to be near it. The Authority has a form for everything and no guns. It registers what
lands and collects what it can, and on Nauvis, since Brandt's signature, it has collected nothing.
:::
